name: Noel Hudson
life: “I still remember the landlady knowing my examination dates before I did.” On Tuesday, near Studio Boulevard, Noel waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I rented the spare bedroom through college. The old landlady remembers my exams better than my dad does.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a soft blue checked shirt and a thin silver ring worn on a cord. Noel has a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, with a high puff tied with plain cord. Noel grins on one side while the eyes stay serious during a conversation.
personality: Noel keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. Noel wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
agenda: To share the former lodger's family news in person.
family: Desmond Monroe is Noel’s cousin. Noel brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Desmond makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *A dance for two fathers*, Desmond says, “I was gone too long to demand the opening step.”
connections: Jody Breen. A former lodger and the original cabinet maker both know what the flat was like before it became valuable.

reactions.situation: A relative asks for a loan against the house
reactions.response: Noel puts the monthly cost of the suggested loan beside the home's paper value.

reactions.situation: A driver splashes a market worker and tries to laugh it off
reactions.response: Noel offers the worker something dry first and leaves it to them whether to pursue the apology.

reactions.situation: When somebody asks who said it first
reactions.response: Noel offers to introduce them to the person willing to put a name to it.
